title: How to do Coan grip
summary: Tutorial on the Coan grip, a one-handed barbell hold from the side learned from Ed Coan. NH uses it for forearm size, not grip strength: it allows progressive overload, isn't CNS taxing, and can be supersetted with leg movements. Set safeties just above the knee, brace with obliques, hold 15 seconds per arm, once every 4-6 days.

claims.claim: NH learned the Coan grip from a video by Ed Coan, whom he calls the greatest powerlifter of all time.
As a bodybuilder he doesn't care about grip strength itself; he uses the Coan grip because it allows easy progressive overload for bigger forearms without taxing the CNS.
The Coan grip can be supersetted with almost any leg movement; NH pairs it with safety-bar squats.
Set the bar on safeties just above the knee so you unrack with minimal movement; the goal is grip work, not bending.
Lifters with a 400-500 lb deadlift can start with a 45 lb plate per side; beginners or those who don't train grip should start with 25s.

numbers.load: 45 lb or 25 lb plates per side

claims.claim: Grab the bar in the middle from the side, not in front of you; hold the rack with the other hand if possible, brace, engage the obliques, get tight, then lift.
For hypertrophy hold about 15 seconds per arm; some do 30 seconds depending on goals. You'll feel an intense forearm stretch.
Do it once every 4-6 days, not daily: the forearm is a small muscle that needs recovery, and hitting it with the same movement daily causes perpetual breakdown without strengthening.
